builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: QMUL_AK at AISA-ArabicFC: Schema-Constrained Function Calling with ALLaM
summary: This replaces generic prompt-only function calling with a LoRA-fine-tuned 7B instruct model using schema-aware prompts, dialect and no-call resampling, a token-weighted loss, and deterministic validation of outputs against the tool schema. Costs are modest: LoRA training of a 7B model fits on a single 24 GB GPU, uses only official task data, and adds a lightweight deterministic validation step at inference, but requires curated task-specific training data and schema definitions. Failures concentrate in argument extraction (0.8920 argument exact match versus 0.9982 function accuracy on the dev set), and results derive from one Arabic shared task, so transfer to other languages, domains, or schema distributions is unverified.
rationale: The approach is feasible on constrained infrastructure and its schema-constrained validation is directly reusable, but the quantified gains come from a single shared-task setting without baselines, so the reader should validate it on their own tool schemas and workloads before production adoption.
technique: LoRA-adapted function calling with schema validation

claims.statement: This replaces generic prompt-only function calling with a LoRA-fine-tuned 7B instruct model using schema-aware prompts, dialect and no-call resampling, a token-weighted loss, and deterministic validation of outputs against the tool schema. Costs are modest: LoRA training of a 7B model fits on a single 24 GB GPU, uses only official task data, and adds a lightweight deterministic validation step at inference, but requires curated task-specific training data and schema definitions. Failures concentrate in argument extraction (0.8920 argument exact match versus 0.9982 function accuracy on the dev set), and results derive from one Arabic shared task, so transfer to other languages, domains, or schema distributions is unverified.

Blind test overall scores of 0.9253 (Track A) and 0.9380 (Track B), 3rd on both tracks, and 1st of 21 teams on the Track C dialect-robustness diagnostic (0.9075 macro score, smallest dialect gap of 0.077); no baseline comparison is reported.
